claims.assertion: The trip contained one off-route segment (18:26–18:38) in which 10.27 km was driven where the optimal route covers 9.43 km, adding 0.84 km and departing up to 2831 m from the optimal route; overall the ride was 16.9 km against a 15.6 km optimal route (+1.3 km).
This is a RydeTAXI trip billed by meter (total $37.66, distance component $23.84 at $1.41/km), so metered-distance overrun from the deviation flows straight into the fare the rider paid.

The rider's own message at 18:10 — “Ok, thanks for telling me.” — is only an acknowledgement of the driver's ECP proposal; it names no route change of the rider's own and does not amount to the rider requesting a stop or a reroute, so no segment is exempted on the rider's request.

The driver's claimed justification is backed by system records: LTA reports an accident at 18:02 on the KPE (towards TPE) at the MCE tunnel entrance with all lanes closed, located 0 m from the optimal route and inside the trip window, and KPE recorded speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 18:00–18:45.

The rider still overpaid the mileage that the deviation added: the fare fact converts the 1.3 km of excess distance to $1.85 (1.3 km × $1.41/km), so at least that sum is a metered overcharge attributable to the longer route.
The driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days (route: 0), so on the record before the court the RD-6 account flag is not triggered by his history.

weaknesses: The driver's reroute is likely exempt under RD-4(a): traffic fact F14 places an LTA-reported accident with all lanes closed 0 m from the optimal route on the KPE/MCE tunnel entrance, reported 18:02, before the off-route segment began at 18:26, and F11 shows KPE at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) through 18:00–18:45 — the driver's own statement (F10) matches this. Chat message F8 (“Ok, thanks for telling me.”, 18:10) sits before the segment start (18:26) and may be read as the rider's agreement to the ECP route under RD-5, which would exempt the segment independently.

The complaint's dollar figure (“about $2 more”) is an estimate, not a system record; the only computable figure is the $1.85 in F4, and F1's total 1.3 km excess exceeds the 0.84 km attributed to the single off-route segment (F3), so part of the excess distance may reflect ordinary matching/route-choice variance rather than the deviation, reducing any recoverable amount.

claims.assertion: The trip contained one off-route segment (18:26–18:38) in which 10.27 km was driven where the optimal route covers 9.43 km, adding 0.84 km and departing up to 2831 m from the optimal route; overall the ride was 16.9 km against a 15.6 km optimal route (+1.3 km).
This is a RydeTAXI trip billed by meter (total $37.66, distance component $23.84 at $1.41/km), so metered-distance overrun from the deviation flows straight into the fare the rider paid.

The rider's own message at 18:10 — “Ok, thanks for telling me.” — is only an acknowledgement of the driver's ECP proposal; it names no route change of the rider's own and does not amount to the rider requesting a stop or a reroute, so no segment is exempted on the rider's request.

The driver's claimed justification is backed by system records: LTA reports an accident at 18:02 on the KPE (towards TPE) at the MCE tunnel entrance with all lanes closed, located 0 m from the optimal route and inside the trip window, and KPE recorded speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 18:00–18:45.

The rider still overpaid the mileage that the deviation added: the fare fact converts the 1.3 km of excess distance to $1.85 (1.3 km × $1.41/km), so at least that sum is a metered overcharge attributable to the longer route.
The driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days (route: 0), so on the record before the court the RD-6 account flag is not triggered by his history.

weaknesses: The driver's reroute is likely exempt under RD-4(a): traffic fact F14 places an LTA-reported accident with all lanes closed 0 m from the optimal route on the KPE/MCE tunnel entrance, reported 18:02, before the off-route segment began at 18:26, and F11 shows KPE at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) through 18:00–18:45 — the driver's own statement (F10) matches this. If that segment is exempted, RD-2 yields no refund for that segment.

Chat message F8 (“Ok, thanks for telling me.”, 18:10) sits before the segment start (18:26) and may be read as the rider's agreement to the ECP route under RD-5, which would exempt the segment independently.

The complaint's dollar figure (“about $2 more”) is an estimate, not a system record; the only computable figure is the $1.85 in F4, and F1's total 1.3 km excess exceeds the 0.84 km attributed to the single off-route segment (F3), so part of the excess distance may reflect ordinary matching/route-choice variance rather than the deviation, reducing any recoverable amount.
The rider's 90-day history shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld (F16), which the other side may use to portray the complaint as repeated rather than manifestly justified.

claims.assertion: The single off-route segment on this RydeTAXI trip (18:26–18:38, 0.84 km extra) is exempt under RD-4(a): an LTA DataMall accident was reported at 18:02 on KPE (towards TPE) at the MCE tunnel entrance, 0 m from the optimal route, all lanes closed, and 18:02 is before the segment start at 18:26 and inside the trip window.

The reroute was also justified by RD-4(a)/(b) corroboration: the substituted optimal-route road KPE was recorded at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 18:00–18:45, while the route actually taken, ECP, was band 7 (60–69 km/h) in the same window, so KPE was not a viable shortest-and-most-direct option.

The rider's own message at 18:10, before the segment began at 18:26, consented to the ECP route: the driver announced the KPE closure at the tunnel entrance and the ECP alternative (F7) and the rider replied "Ok, thanks for telling me." (F8); under RD-5 the segment therefore also falls outside the deviation finding, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F9).

The driver's written statement (F10) matches the system records rather than contradicting them: he reported the KPE accident closure and the ECP reroute, consistent with the 18:02 accident record (F14) and the KPE band-1 congestion (F11), so nothing in the statement needs to be discounted.

No excess fare is attributable to the exempted segment: the billed excess is $1.85 for 1.3 km at $1.41/km (F4), and with the sole off-route segment exempt the extra distance refundable under RD-2 is 0, so the correct outcome is no_action on the fare; the remaining distance/time figures (F6) reflect the metered trip at 1.0× with no surge (F5) and no waiting charge (F6).

The rider's complaint that the fare exceeded the estimate rests on the trip taking 32.5 min against a 21 min estimate (F2), but the delay is explained by the 18:02 KPE accident and band-1 congestion (F14, F11) plus light rain (F15), not by any unexplained deviation; the only deviation is the exempted one.

No flag_account should attach to this driver: the profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F17), so the RD-6 condition of a prior upheld route dispute is not met, and this case itself is not upheld.

The RD-4(b) band evidence alone is not an independent exemption ground (it operates only as corroboration for RD-4(a)), so my defence rests primarily on the 0 m, 18:02 accident record (F14).
